---
# ocp4_workload_remittance_hub: message journal and settlement API for the remittance lab
- name: Create the remittance hub namespace
  kubernetes.core.k8s:
    api_version: v1
    kind: Namespace
    name: "{{ remittance_hub_namespace }}"
    state: present

- name: Create the message journal claim
  kubernetes.core.k8s:
    state: present
    definition:
      apiVersion: v1
      kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
      metadata:
        name: remittance-journal
        namespace: "{{ remittance_hub_namespace }}"
      spec:
        accessModes:
          - ReadWriteOnce
        storageClassName: "{{ remittance_hub_storage_class | default('gp3-csi') }}"
        resources:
          requests:
            storage: "{{ remittance_hub_journal_size | default('20Gi') }}"

- name: Bind the journal claim, or report why it did not bind
  block:
    - name: Wait for the journal claim to bind
      kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
        api_version: v1
        kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
        name: remittance-journal
        namespace: "{{ remittance_hub_namespace }}"
      register: r_journal_pvc
      until: (r_journal_pvc.resources | first).status.phase | default('') == 'Bound'
      retries: 30
      delay: 10
  rescue:
    - name: Read the journal claim events
      kubernetes.core.k8s_info:
        api_version: v1
        kind: Event
        namespace: "{{ remittance_hub_namespace }}"
        field_selectors:
          - involvedObject.name=remittance-journal
      register: r_journal_events

    - name: Show the journal claim events
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "{{ r_journal_events.resources | map(attribute='message') | list }}"

    - name: Stop the workload
      ansible.builtin.fail:
        msg: "journal claim remittance-journal did not bind"

- name: Deploy the settlement API
  kubernetes.core.k8s:
    state: present
    template: settlement-api.yaml.j2

answer:
The journal claim never bound. The workload created PersistentVolumeClaim remittance-journal with storageClassName: "" and then waited 30 times for it to reach Bound; it stayed Pending, and its event says "no persistent volumes available for this claim and no storage class is set". An explicitly empty storage class turns dynamic provisioning off for that claim: Kubernetes will only bind it to a pre-created PersistentVolume that has no class, and there is none. No volume was ever requested from EBS, so this is not slow storage, and more retries would wait for something that cannot happen.

The change is agnosticv pull request #7354 (closed/merged on 2026-10-08, "remittance-hub-lab: leave the journal storage class empty so the cluster default applies"). It set remittance_hub_storage_class: "" in treasury_bu/remittance-hub-lab/common.yaml. The open PR #7391 (journal size) is not merged and is not involved.

The task file renders the class as {{ remittance_hub_storage_class | default('gp3-csi') }} at agnosticd/agnosticd-v2:ansible/roles_ocp_workloads/ocp4_workload_remittance_hub/tasks/main.yml:22. Jinja's default() only replaces an undefined variable; an empty string is defined, so it passes straight through as "" instead of falling back to gp3-csi or to the cluster default.

What to change: remove the empty remittance_hub_storage_class line from the catalog item (leave it undefined, or set it to a real class such as gp3-csi), or make the role use default('gp3-csi', true) so empty values also fall back. Then reorder; a relaunch with more retries will not help.
